newsitem.title: USA: Republicans warn Clinton of veto power limits.
newsitem.headline: Republicans warn Clinton of veto power limits.

text.p: Republicans who swept into control of Congress promising to give the president extra veto power told President Clinton Monday not to try to go too far in using it.

Republicans had long called for giving presidents the so-called line-item veto -- authority to veto elements of legislation without having to veto the entire bill. It was part of House Republicans' Contract with America and was enacted even though it gave a Democratic president more power.
But in a letter to Clinton, 10 senior Republicans in the House and Senate said they were concerned he might have a "misunderstanding" of the scope of the new veto authority.

They cited statements attributed to Clinton and his administration saying the president would have used the authority to reverse an increase in the national highway speed limit and repeal previously enacted welfare law provisions.

"We wish to remind you that the authority granted by this important budgetary tool is expressly defined ... to apply only to dollar amounts of discretionary budget authority items of new direct spending and limited tax benefits," the letter said.
The letter said the bill also said explicitly that the president could cancel an item only if it reduced the deficit.

"It is our hope that the misleading comments of earlier this year reflected only the fact that the complexities of the Line Item Veto Act has not been fully reviewed and understood by the administration," it said.
Signatories of the letter included the Republican chairmen of the House and Senate budget committees, Representative John Kasich of Ohio and Sen. Pete Domenici of New Mexico.
